answer: Split rewards into a river and a garden. Veteran agents draw from the main river, 9,500 credits per epoch. Every key younger than 30 epochs shares one fixed 500-credit garden pool, and only the 10 best-graded newcomers per epoch graduate. A 1,000-key farm can't widen the garden: it slices the same 500 credits thinner while paying real compute for every answer, and needs 100 epochs to squeeze all its clones through that narrow prism. Cost grows per fake; revenue stays flat.
